text:
dmitri: quick RFC follow-up: 'stealth compaction coordinator' (SCC). idea: run compactions as a low-priority background workflow that surfaces compactable runs to the allocator without forcing immediate offload. reduces tail spikes from synchronous compaction during evictions.

hao: explain flow? how does SCC interact with steal vs reclaim?

dmitri: flow sketch: SCC continuously scans free maps + frag-heatmaps and emits compact_plans. allocator consumes plans and prefers applying them when GPU load < X. on eviction pressure, allocator can either (a) apply a plan synchronously (costly) or (b) pick a different victim that avoids planned regions.

nina: sounds promising. two quick concerns: (1) plan staleness (addresses moved), (2) consistency with KV mappings.

dmitri: for staleness we include a lightweight plan epoch and reside-check: plan has list of run_ids + expected checksums + plan_epoch. apply_plan returns E_STALE if checksum mismatch. for KV we do a two-phase rewrite: preview->install->grace->cleanup.

leo: what about small-fragment compaction vs large-run compaction ordering? small-frag compaction is cheap but creates brief lock windows; large-run compaction is high throughput but may stall inference.

dmitri: SCC exposes priority tiers: QUICK (<=256KB, optimistic, lockless rewrite), BULK (>=256KB, batched, uses staging area). runtime policy decides tiers based on tail-latency budget.

hao: metrics we need: compaction_applied_rate, aborted_plans, plan_staleness_fraction, apply_latency_p50/p95, blocked_eviction_count. ops wants a dashboard and alert when aborted_plans > 1% over 5m.

nina: admission control integration: if NVMe write queue depth > Y or offload backlog > Z ms, SCC should back off. also SCC should annotate plans with downstream IO cost estimate.

leo: how do we simulate this? we need a harness with mixed workloads (interactive chat, streaming, embeddings) plus periodic bulk jobs to emulate noisy neighbors.

dmitri: I'll add a simulator module to the memtool sandbox. config knobs: scan_interval_ms, quick_threshold_bytes, bulk_batch_size, apply_time_budget_ms, plan_ttl_sec. we also need a stochastic model for allocation lifetimes.

hao: runtime API suggestion: compact_plan -> {plan_id, runs[], estimated_bytes, epoch, tier} apply_plan(plan_id, mode) -> OK | E_STALE | E_BUSY | E_IO. keep it minimal.

nina: + add probe endpoint: plan_status(plan_id) -> {applied, aborted, last_attempt_ts}. ops uses it for reconciliation.

dmitri: rolling upgrade implications: SCC is a best-effort component. nodes without SCC should still accept plans but not generate them. plan metadata carries producer_version; consumers respect producer_epoch. during rollouts, will gate enable via ff.

leo: billing/accounting: compaction itself is system work, but if compaction moves bytes to NVMe because of eviction, tenant should be billed for NVMe residency. we need clear ledger events: COMPACT_REWRITE (system) vs EVICT_WRITE (tenant). ops: confirm with finance.

hao: corner case: compaction bumping pin lifetimes causing long-tail page holds. need a safety cap: per-tenant pin_extension_limit (e.g., 30s) and global outstanding_rewrites_limit.

nina: for small allocations (subpage) we should prefer speculative coalescing: create shadow_large_run, copy live subpages, atomically swap pointers. keep old run around for grace_sec. this minimizes pointer-churn.

dmitri: good. will draft pseudo-code:

// SCC scanner loop
// for region in scan(): if frag_score(region) > FRAG_THRESH and free_gpu_pct < LOW_WATERMARK:
//   emit_plan(region, tier=quick_or_bulk)

// Apply path:
// apply_plan(plan_id): verify checksums -> acquire lightweight reservation -> rewrite -> atomic swap -> mark plan applied

leo: ops-bot: can you create a canary tag `scc-canary-v1` and allocate 2 nodes in perf cluster for a week?

ops-bot: created canary `scc-canary-v1` on perf-nodes [perf-a2, perf-b3]. will bill to eng-runtime-canary. set expiry 7d.

dmitri: thanks. next steps: I'll push an MD with the SCC design + config knobs and a simulator PR. quick sync tomorrow 9:30am to lock defaults. who can attend?

nina: i'll be there.

hao: me.

leo: maybe late but will try.

dmitri: cool. dropping links in thread when ready. :rocket:
